g.text: One step of a faulted trusted history on real files
The live chain takes the fault; a byte copy admitted cold, a fault-free reference chain
and an in-memory oracle store judge its outcome before the next step
settled point: the live catalog file holds the core's image, the
index length is its appointed tail, and the live and reference
stores hold the same files and cores with equal observations
normalize the drawn fault and interleave to what the settled
store admits: a corrupt sidecar needs a pending reclamation
intent, an unpin needs a reader, a refusal needs a change
run the interleave: refusals that change no file, a reader pin
or unpin, a lease counter at its maximum, a fresh generation
checkpoint, a crash in the middle of reclamation, an idle
foreign catalog, a restart, a bind of a past version, or a
decoy bound to the store's pathname
bind and prepare the step's transition: a jump to a slot
configuration, a path edit, or a revert to an earlier state;
the reference chain publishes it without a fault
arm the fault: a failpoint at one of the hooks 2 to 14, an I/O
failpoint, a torn slot prefix, a short pack, a corrupt sidecar,
a replaced catalog, a catalog changed at the compare, or a
decoy at the re-read
publish_trusted_incremental_v1 on the live chain: the hook trace
is the publication order up to the fault, with no cold
admission and no index construction

The independent judge
The copy shares no lease, registry or process
state with the live writer. Its observation is
compared, never its bytes after admission: its
fresh registry may reclaim what the live
writer's reader still defers.
copy the store byte for byte into a fresh directory and admit
the copy cold, with its own writer lease and lease registry;
every object of its current closure must read the oracle's
bytes, and a corrupt sidecar or a foreign catalog is refused
stale retry of the same prepared publication from
the stale core: refused at the catalog compare with no
hook when the catalog changed, or at the index length
check when an indeterminate write kept the old slot

or recover through the held lease, which rebuilds the index,
or restart and admit cold by path, or repair a foreign catalog
compare the settled core with the copy's, observation for

the oracle, the closures, the pinned reader's prefixes and
the keep-all retention history
